claims.claim: Critic Ray Davis comments that Wolfe is simply not managing to do the job he wants to do.
claims.source: Ray Davis in comments on Waggish, 8 December 2007
claims.quote: he’s simply not managing to do the job he wants to do

claims.claim: The reviewer bormgans reports that on rereading The Book of the New Sun was to a certain extent a lesser affair than he remembered.
claims.source: bormgans, 'THE BOOK OF THE NEW SUN - Gene Wolfe (1980-83)', Weighing a pig doesn't fatten it, 16 May 2021
claims.quote: I have to admit that to a certain extent is was

claims.claim: bormgans calls Peter Wright's Ultan's Library review a rather hagiographic text.
claims.source: bormgans on Peter Wright's review, Weighing a pig doesn't fatten it, 16 May 2021
claims.quote: has written a rather hagiographic text on the subject

claims.claim: bormgans relays Marc Aramini's observation that critical discourse on Wolfe is marked by how infrequently any two people agree with each other.
claims.source: bormgans quoting Marc Aramini's review of Andre-Driussi's Chapter Guide (2019), Weighing a pig doesn't fatten it, 16 May 2021
claims.quote: how infrequently any two people will agree with each other
claims.page: section on the three reasons interpretation is difficult

claims.claim: bormgans writes in the comments that there is something of a one-trick pony vibe to Wolfe's writing.
claims.source: bormgans in comments, Weighing a pig doesn't fatten it, 17 May 2021
claims.quote: there’s something of a one-trick pony vibe to his writing

claims.claim: A commenter says reviews of this kind keep them shying away from Gene Wolfe.
claims.source: commenter 'Riders of Skaith', Weighing a pig doesn't fatten it, 17 May 2021
claims.quote: It’s reviews like like this that keep me shying away

claims.claim: The reviewer Jesse calls The Book of the New Sun divisive for its relative opacity.
Keller says Wolfe's themes are buried in long-winded sentences.
claims.source: Alex Keller, Innsmouth Free Press, 31 August 2009
claims.quote: themes are so buried in long-winded sentences

claims.claim: Keller says Wolfe's descriptive style buries the story in dense descriptions and slowing adjectives that make the text difficult to read.
claims.source: Alex Keller, Innsmouth Free Press, 31 August 2009
claims.quote: burying it in dense descriptions and slowing adjectives
claims.page: section on The Death of Doctor Island

claims.claim: Algis Budrys wrote that one cannot take full satisfaction in The Shadow of the Torturer because no one part of the tetralogy is whole.
claims.source: Algis Budrys, "Books: 'The Shadow of the Torturer'", The Magazine of Fantasy and Science Fiction, vol. 58 no. 5, May 1980, pp. 26-7, reprinted in Contemporary Literary Criticism vol. 25

claims.claim: Budrys wrote that Wolfe is asking readers to read what will eventually be a quarter-million words while waiting for the full reward.
claims.source: Algis Budrys, F&SF, vol. 58 no. 5, May 1980, pp. 26-7, reprinted in CLC vol. 25
claims.quote: a quarter-million words while waiting for the full reward

claims.claim: Thomas Disch wrote that science fantasy strikes him as inauthentic, coy and trivial even when practised by writers he admires.
claims.source: Thomas M. Disch, 'A Wizard of the Fabulous', Book World - The Washington Post, 22 March 1981, p. 11, reprinted in CLC vol. 25
claims.quote: science fantasy strikes me as inauthentic, coy, and trivial

claims.claim: Disch says chapters in The Claw of the Conciliator venture perilously close to pulp magazine hugger-mugger.
claims.source: Thomas M. Disch, Book World - The Washington Post, 22 March 1981, p. 11, reprinted in CLC vol. 25
claims.quote: venture perilously close to pulp magazine hugger-mugger

claims.claim: Disch says one long interpolated masque in The Claw of the Conciliator is too archly Significant, after the manner of Thornton Wilder's The Skin of Our Teeth.
claims.source: Thomas M. Disch, Book World - The Washington Post, 22 March 1981, p. 11, reprinted in CLC vol. 25
claims.quote: that are too archly Significant, after the manner of Thornton

claims.claim: Disch argues that in allegorical fantasy each element must bear a weight of meditated meaning that deepens as the tale progresses, and says Wolfe achieves this.
claims.source: Thomas M. Disch, Book World - The Washington Post, 22 March 1981, p. 11, reprinted in CLC vol. 25
claims.quote: bears a weight of meditated meaning that intensifies and deepens

verdicts.trueWording: he's simply not managing to do the job he wants
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'Critic' — the page identifies Ray Davis only as a commenter, never as a critic
verdicts.note: Live page fetched raw (HTTP 200). Quote is word-for-word in the comment signed 'Ray Davis 8 December 2007 at 06:47' under David Auerbach's 7 December 2007 post, in the 6-comment thread. Only the appositive 'Critic' is unsupported by this page; the substance and attribution to Ray Davis are exact.

verdicts.trueWording: I have to admit that to a certain extent is was
verdicts.note: Live page fetched raw (HTTP 200), post 'Posted on May 16, 2021'. Opening section: he feared the book would be a lesser affair than remembered and admits it partly was. Page's own typo 'is was' reproduced. Context limb not in claim: he adds it did not become a bad book and still ranks among his favourite reads.

verdicts.trueWording: has written a rather hagiographic text on the subject
verdicts.note: Live page raw. Sentence reads 'Peter Wright has written a rather hagiographic text on the subject', in the section on obscure diction/lexicons. The page word is 'article', hyperlinked to https://ultan.org.uk/review-botns/ — i.e. the Ultan's Library piece — so the claim's 'Ultan's Library review' is carried by the href on the raw page rather than by the visible text.

verdicts.trueWording: how infrequently any two people will agree with each other
verdicts.note: Live page raw. Appears twice, both times as bormgans quoting 'Wolfe scholar Marc Aramini' from his review of Michael Andre-Driussi's 'Gene Wolfe: The Book of the New Sun: A Chapter Guide (2019)'. Every limb (relay, Aramini, critical discourse, 2019 Chapter Guide review) is on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: there's something of a one-trick pony vibe to his writing
verdicts.note: Live page raw. In the comment signed 'bormgans | May 17, 2021 at 14:35', replying to Riders of Skaith; sentence ends '...to his writing too.' A separate bormgans comment (14:53) uses the near-variant 'one-trick pony quality to certain aspects of his writing' — the claim's wording matches the 14:35 comment.

verdicts.trueWording: reviews like like this that keep me shying away
verdicts.note: Live page raw. Comment signed 'Riders of Skaith | May 17, 2021 at 14:29': the doubled 'like like' is the page's own. Full sentence names Gene Wolfe. Claim's generic 'A commenter' is supported.

Live page raw (blogspot, HTTP 200), post dated Monday, July 9, 2012, 'Posted by Jesse'. Opening paragraph: after naming the four volumes it runs 'Divisive for its relative opacity, there remains a very simple formula...'. Subject is Wolfe's Book of the New Sun; reviewer name and date both on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: themes are so buried in long-winded sentences
verdicts.note: Live page raw. Byline 'by Alex Keller', dated August 31, 2009. Opening paragraph: 'Wolfe's themes are so buried in long-winded sentences, and are so over-intellectualized...'. All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: burying it in dense descriptions and slowing adjectives
verdicts.note: Live page raw. In the section on 'The Death of Doctor Island', immediately after a quoted sample sentence: 'I find it detracts from, rather than enhances, the story, burying it in dense descriptions and slowing adjectives that make the text difficult to read.' The antecedent 'This style' is the style of the quoted descriptive passage, so the claim's 'descriptive style' is fair.

enotes.com returned HTTP 403 to both plain and browser-UA requests; recovered via Wayback raw capture 20241114002444id_ (HTTP 200, full criticism text). Page: 'The difficulty with taking full satisfaction with The Shadow of the Torturer is that one can't; ... no one part is whole.' Citation block confirms F&SF Vol. 58 No. 5, May 1980, pp. 26-7, in CLC Vol. 25. Nuance: Budrys resists the word 'tetralogy', calling it 'one book with four aspects'.

verdicts.trueWording: a quarter-million words while waiting for the full reward
verdicts.note: Same Wayback raw capture (20241114002444id_). Page: 'he is asking us to read what will no doubt eventually be a quarter-million words while waiting for the full reward.' Claim's 'eventually' and 'full reward' both on the page; Budrys then adds he thinks Wolfe deserves that trust.

verdicts.trueWording: science fantasy strikes me as inauthentic, coy, and trivial
verdicts.note: enotes.com HTTP 403 live; recovered via Wayback raw capture 20250914044440id_ (HTTP 200). Page: 'Even when practiced by writers I ordinarily admire—Ursula Le Guin, Michael Moorcock, Brian Aldiss—science fantasy strikes me as inauthentic, coy, and trivial...'. Citation confirms Book World—The Washington Post, March 22, 1981, p. 11.

verdicts.trueWording: venture perilously close to pulp magazine hugger-mugger
verdicts.note: Same Wayback raw capture (20250914044440id_). Page: 'There are chapters in The Claw of the Conciliator that venture perilously close to pulp magazine hugger-mugger'. Framed by Disch's concession that any tetralogy's second volume comes off second-best.

verdicts.trueWording: too archly Significant, after the manner of Thornton Wilder's
verdicts.note: Same Wayback raw capture. Page: 'other chapters—one long interpolated masque, in particular—that are too archly Significant, after the manner of Thornton Wilder's The Skin of Our Teeth.' Capital S on 'Significant' is the page's own; Disch adds that Wolfe resembles Wilder in happier respects.

verdicts.trueWording: bears a weight of meditated meaning that intensifies and deepens
verdicts.note: Same Wayback raw capture. Page: intensity and depth in allegorical fantasy are possible only if each element 'bears a weight of meditated meaning that intensifies and deepens as the tale progresses'. The second limb is supported two sentences on: 'Wolfe, however, is a Wagnerian, not a tree trimmer; his allegory actually has something to say.'
